answer: The credential is a tide-gauge residual: one calibrated sensor per seat, bolted to a pier, serial etched on the housing. It logs four minutes past the seed's mark, and the ledger subtracts the port's harmonic prediction, keeping a residual wind surge drives. Replaying the tide table scores zero; the figure must sit within three centimetres of the next gauge. Two seats on one pier fold to one vote and forfeit 45,000 POA; sensors cost $1,200, a thousand clones need a thousand piers. A beacon sweeps the water nightly; a lantern on the horizon marks a channel only real swell lets a hull read.
